work_completed: Phase 1 (core types + Ed25519 sign/verify) across crates/nlt-toi and go/nlt-toi, cross-validated against the TS/Python references (packages/toi/src/sign.ts, src/nlt_toi/sign.py).

Rust (crates/nlt-toi/src/lib.rs): added ToiKeyPair, generate_key_pair, signing_payload, sign_toi, verify_toi, is_signed, plus a dependency-free unpadded base64url codec (base64url_encode/base64url_decode with canonical-trailing-bit validation). Cargo.toml: rand_core enabled with getrandom for OsRng seed generation.
Go (go/nlt-toi/sign.go): added ToiKeyPair, GenerateKeyPair, SigningPayload, SignToi, VerifyToi, IsSigned on crypto/ed25519 + base64.RawURLEncoding.

Corrected the ToiSignature envelope in both ports to {alg, public_key, value} per toiSignatureSchema (was signature/signed_at, which would have produced non-conformant envelopes). verify_toi/VerifyToi are fully defensive (never throw/panic), reject padded or whitespaced base64url per SPEC §11.1, and return false for un-canonicalizable input.
Signed payload is always canonicalize(document without $signature) as UTF-8 — identical semantics to TS/Python.

Tests: 13 new Rust signing tests (30 total green) and 12 new Go signing tests (31 total green), mirroring sign.test.ts/test_sign.py including: round-trip, tamper detection, reformat/key-reorder stability, payload==canonicalize(doc), committed known-answer fixture, wrong-key rejection, malformed/padded/whitespaced base64url, wrong-length signature bytes, non-canonical trailing-bit rejection, and the deterministic vector.

Cross-runtime proof: both Rust and Go verify the committed JS-produced signed.toi fixture byte-for-byte, and both produce identical envelope bytes for the shared deterministic vector (seed 1..=32, minimal payload): public_key ebVWLo_mVPlAeLES6KmLp5AfhTrmlb7X4OORC60ElmQ, signature ubQpn9BdJH6yVrX_XWUA2KhoSi3_hBzfD_5z_xISH6PV_UfKvvNfjuq8icQww79NUPlkNVaSGnQKbs6z04QHBg — matching the TS/Python reference output. The seed key matches the committed fixture's public key.

Applied nlt-code-reviewer feedback (APPROVE_WITH_NITS) from the phase-gate review: Go base64url now rejects non-canonical trailing padding bits via re-encode check (was lenient — the only conformance divergence from TS/Python/Rust); Rust sign_toi returns ToiError::InvalidDocument for non-object input instead of silently returning the unsigned copy; ToiKeyPair Debug now redacts the private seed; SignToi checks the object shape before canonicalizing; CHANGELOG vector wording tightened.
Reference suites unaffected: TS vitest 65 passed, Python pytest 65 passed.
Governance validation: bash .nltotoi/scripts/validate-governance.sh — 29 passed, 0 failed. gofmt clean; Rust builds warning-free.
Updated CHANGELOG.md (Unreleased → Added) and docs/active-threads.md (new NLT-TOI-PHASE1-SIGNING thread).
work_in_progress: Phase 1 PR open for review/merge on GitHub (branch cto/phase1-ed25519-signing). Phase gate: run nlt-code-reviewer before merging.
decisions_made: Phase 1 scope (approved by Joshua): envelope fix + sign/verify only — implement sign/verify at the JSON-value level and correct ToiSignature to {alg, public_key, value}; defer full ToiDocument schema re-model to the validation phase.
Rust generate_key_pair uses rand_core::OsRng (getrandom) to produce the 32-byte seed, then ed25519-dalek SigningKey::from_bytes — avoids enabling ed25519-dalek's rand_core feature.

Deterministic cross-runtime vector uses seed bytes 1..=32 (matches the committed fixture's public key) so Rust/Go tests assert byte-for-byte identity with the reference output, not just behavioral equivalence.
Rust skips the 'non-canonicalizable content' verify case (serde_json cannot represent NaN/Infinity); Go covers it with math.Inf via json.Marshal failure.
decisions_pending: Whether Phase 2 should re-model the typed ToiDocument to the canonical schema + add parse/schema validation and resolve() in Rust/Go.
handoff_record.next_agent_notes: Run nlt-code-reviewer on the Phase 1 PR at the phase gate, then merge via squash with the validated commit convention. After merge, Phase 2 options per the port plan: typed schema validation (parse), ToiDocument schema re-model, and the resolve()/tier-precedence layer — cross-validated against packages/toi and src/nlt_toi. The deterministic vector constants and the signed.toi fixture are the canonical cross-runtime signing vectors to reuse for any future runtime port.
